Found a real gap: original AppGroupCache.get() treated an expired entry as a miss but never deleted it, so stale entries accumulated forever, and since cleanup only fired reactively on a get() for that exact key, a never-revisited location would never get cleaned up. Fixed with two mechanisms: (1) expired entries deleted both reactively on get() and proactively across every entry on each put(). (2) hard cap on entry count (maxRetainedEntries=10), evicting oldest-by-fetchedAt when exceeded -- TTL alone only bounds age not count. Added SharedCacheStore.allKeys() so AppGroupCache can enumerate/sweep its own prefixed entries without touching a shared store's other data. File protection: verified against Apple's own Security Guide that macOS has no per-file Data Protection classes like iOS -- Class A is backed by the FileVault volume key on macOS, Class D is unsupported. RefreshScheduler derives a stable per-install offset within the refresh interval (persisted via SharedCacheStore, so container app and widget see the same schedule) and computes the next refresh time on that install's interval-spaced schedule -- spreading load across installs instead of everyone waking at the top of the hour. AQICacheEntry now carries softExpiresAt/hardExpiresAt (was one expiresAt) plus AQIFreshness (.fresh/.stale/.expired) and freshness(at:). AppGroupCache.get()/getCurrentLocation() now return a reading through the stale window, only going nil past the hard threshold -- previously they went nil at the single TTL, which is what produced the 2.826s blocking-fetch case measured for Marlton in bluegull-aqi-mtm.23. Added freshness(for:)/currentLocationFreshness()/mostRecentEntryFreshness(), all nil past hard expiry (a real bug in my own first pass -- they returned .expired instead of nil, caught by testCurrentLocationFreshnessMirrorsGetCurrentLocation failing). Defaults: soft=1hr (AirNow's own cadence, matches the pre-existing single TTL so request volume is unchanged), hard=3hr (fallback window). WidgetTimelineSnapshot/BluegullAQIWidgetEntry now carry freshness end-to-end using the same location-specified-vs-fallback cascade shape as reading itself.

Deliberately NOT implemented: active background revalidation of a stale entry. The widget only fetches when reading is nil (absent or hard-expired); a stale-but-present entry is returned as-is with no refetch triggered from the widget process. This is an accepted, disclosed gap, not an oversight -- a fire-and-forget Task in the widget extension is unreliable (the process can be suspended immediately after returning its Timeline, per doc/DESIGN.md ​4.3's own documented constraint), and rebuilding a proactive revalidation loop in the container app would partially undo bluegull-aqi-mtm.24's cleanup from earlier today. In practice: the menu bar's own displayed location still revalidates every runLoop cycle (~hourly) regardless; other locations only a widget looks at stay visibly-aged until something else re-fetches them (a hard expiry blocking-fetch, or coincidental other traffic).
